title: NextBundleManifest
description: A compiled course bundle in the shape the lexical model needs (docs/migration-design.md, deliverable 3): format version 2. It has lexemes, feature values and rules where a bundle had KCs, and its tokens list the lexemes they write. Written by the compiler from a language's lexicon and a course in the new shape; at the flip it replaces bundle.schema.json and the `Next` names lose their prefix. What did not change is referenced from that file.

formatVersion.description: 2: lexemes where a bundle had KCs (ADR 0145). An app that does not know the version keeps the bundle it has and asks to be updated.

id.description: sha256 of the manifest without this field.

lexicon.description: The language whose lexicon the course draws on (ADR 0145: one lexicon per language). A part's id is unique in it.

variety.description: The variety the course teaches, where it names one (ADR 0147: a dialect tag is derived from it).

registers.description: The registers the course teaches, where it names them.

names.description: What the app calls the course and its orthographies, as the course source names them (ADR 0109). Also in the bundles' index.json, for a list of courses.

facets.description: The facets the course practises, where it names them (course source `facets`, ADR 0071); absent: all of them.

audioQuality.description: How far learners may rely on the course's clips, where it is not good (course source `audio.quality`, ADR 0091). iffy: no template whose prompt is a clip (listening, listen-and-repeat) is planned; clips still play where the learner has the text. A bad voice ships no clips, so it needs no flag.

placement.description: How the placement test probes, where the course says (course source `placement`, ADR 0077).

wordParts.description: The course asks words by their parts (course source `wordParts`, ADR 0152): the templates `parts-whole` and `whole-parts` are planned. Absent: they are not.

versions.description: Everything that can change the output: schema, Unicode and CLDR data, analyzers, ICU.

files.description: Every file in the bundle by role, with its SPDX license.

credits.description: Attribution, once per bundle (ADR 0110): each text a file or clip credits (a recording's speaker, a synthetic voice and what it cloned, a table's or picture's source), by its id, the first 8 hex digits of the text's sha256. Files and clips name it by that id (`credit`).

units.description: The units in path order. Each is a download unit for offline use (gameplan §16 Phase 10): its JSON is part of the course, which every device keeps, and `assets` are the media (audio and images) its items use, downloaded per unit.

licenses.description: SPDX expression → number of content items.

provenance.description: Counts by status and author kind.

release.description: A release build (ADR 0073): only content a reviewer signed off. Absent in the demo's full builds, which keep drafts.

role.description: lexicon: the course's lexemes, labels and named rules (BundleLexicon), one file. aliases: what each KC id of the course became (aliases.schema.json), which upgrading a log written before format version 2 reads.

credit.description: Who or what made the file (its source): an entry of the manifest's `credits`.

bytes.description: Size in bytes, to say what a download costs before it starts.

BundleLexicon.title: BundleLexicon
BundleLexicon.description: The course's part of its language's lexicon (role lexicon): every lexeme a node of the course introduces or a token of it writes, in one list sorted by id. It is flat (the owner, 2026-11-20): no entry says which unit teaches it, and a unit's nodes point at it. With it, what a learner is shown for the feature values the course's tokens carry and for the rules its nodes and sentences name.

labels.description: The names of feature values, alone or several together (the language's `labels`). The most specific label whose values a form has names it.

rules.description: The rules the course names (the language's `rules`), each with what a learner is shown for it.

BundleLexeme.title: BundleLexeme
BundleLexeme.description: One lexeme as a course ships it. What kind it is shows in what it has, as in the lexicon: a part of speech, `realises` (a value head: uz -ga) or `head` (a function head). A form a rule gives and ours does not yet (pinned) is not here: it is stored and checked in the lexicon, and never a learner's part (ADR 0146).

feats.description: Its lexical features, every one: what its entry stores and what a default of its language gives (mano and casa are both Gender Fem here). A choice that asks which lexeme offers only lexemes with the answer's part of speech and these, exactly (ADR 0132).

chooses.description: Lexical features of its category that its tokens choose instead (hermano, whose tokens are masculine or feminine).

parts.description: Its parts beyond itself (ADR 0146: every part no rule gives): a lexical feature no default gives (lexeme:mano|Gender), a listed form or stem, a class, a leftover of an orthography. A lexeme with none is learned once itself is.

forms.description: How it is written, per orthography: its entry's spellings, the first the one a card shows, then those of its allomorphs. Each with the readings and vowel marks the course pins.

image.description: Bundle path of its picture (a file with role image).

BundleLabel.title: BundleLabel
BundleLabel.description: The name of a set of feature values (language.schema.json FeatureLabel), per support language: preterite, I (Tense=Past, Person=1, Number=Sing). `pos` narrows it to one category.

BundleRule.title: BundleRule
BundleRule.description: A rule the course names, with what a learner is shown for it. Until rules are written (docs/migration-design.md, "Not designed here") a rule is its name and its gloss: what a `construction:` KC was.

BundleGrapheme.title: BundleGrapheme
BundleGrapheme.description: A letter, a digraph or a mark a script track teaches (ADR 0149: a grapheme stays the track's, never the lexicon's): how each orthography writes it, and in a Latin orthography what a track asks it as (ADR 0133).

NextBundleUnit.title: NextBundleUnit
NextBundleUnit.description: A unit's file. It defines no lexemes: its nodes point at the bundle's lexicon. The letters its script nodes teach are the one thing it lists.

NextScriptItem.title: NextScriptItem
NextScriptItem.description: A letter or a lexeme of an alphabet node: what it is, how the orthography writes it, and its reading in Latin letters (ADR 0133): a lexeme's pinned reading in its track's scheme's `latin`, a letter as that scheme writes it.

id.description: The letter (a grapheme id) or the lexeme.

letters.description: The letters it is written with, of those its track teaches (a letter: its own).

introduces.description: What the node teaches for the first time: lexemes, feature values, rules, and a script node's letters. The one place the teaching order is written.

alphabet.description: An alphabet node's letters and practice lexemes, each with its reading in Latin letters (ADR 0088, 0133).

BundleTag.title: BundleTag
BundleTag.description: One tag of a prompt (ADR 0147): what the answer must say and the prompt leaves open. A value from a closed set, rendered from the UI catalog (persons, register, variety), or an authored situation in each support language. Exactly one of the four. A variety is derived by the compiler from the course's and is never authored.

parts.description: Every part the sentence can give evidence of (ADR 0146), each once: the lexemes its tokens write, the feature values they carry that a node of the course introduces, the rules it is an example of (the source's `uses`), and a lexeme's own part where a token shows it (mano's gender, on the article that agrees with it).

tags.description: What the answer must say and the prompt leaves open (ADR 0147), shown under the prompt where the answer's language marks it.

NextBundleStory.title: NextBundleStory
NextBundleStory.description: A compiled story (Phase 6): its lines in every orthography of the course, translations and questions in every support language.

speaker.description: The character's gender as a speaker, where the course sets it (ADR 0078).

parts.description: Every part its lines can give evidence of.

gap.description: complete: the lexeme the line leaves out and asks for.

options.description: complete: the wrong options as the compiler resolved them (ADR 0132), each per orthography: one token the course writes in the story's unit or earlier (another lexeme in the gap's form, or the gap's lexeme in another form), analysis and readings kept.

NextBundleAudio.title: NextBundleAudio
NextBundleAudio.description: audio.json (role audio-index): playable clips by item. An item is a sentence's id, a story line's (`story#step`), a lexeme's id for its entry's spelling, or a form's key for a clip that says one form of a lexeme or a token built of several (common.schema.json FormKey).
